subject: ela
intro: Seventh graders analyze the structure an author uses to organize a text, including how major sections contribute to the whole and to the development of the ideas. Common structures include chronological, cause and effect, compare and contrast, problem and solution, and question and answer. Headings and sections guide the reader.

items.prompt:
Read.

Section 1 describes the problem of plastic pollution. Section 2 explains its causes. Section 3 proposes solutions.

What overall structure does the text use?

steps: I look at how the sections relate.
It presents a problem, its causes, and solutions.
So the structure is problem and solution (with cause and effect).
solution.answer: Problem and solution (with cause and effect).

items.prompt: How does the 'solutions' section contribute to the whole text?

steps: Each section builds on the last.
The solutions section answers the problem raised earlier.
So it completes the argument by responding to the problem.
solution.answer: It responds to the problem, completing the text's argument.

items.prompt: A text organized by dates from 1900 to 2000 uses what structure?

steps: Events in time order is chronological.

items.prompt: Headings tell the reader what each ____ is about.
